subject.title: [Feature]: Audit log for agent memory changes

question: Should OpenClaw implement memory-file mutation audit as a bundled memory-core/core write-surface contract, a generic plugin persistence hook, or defer it to external memory/MCP plugins?
rationale: The issue affects memory trust and tamper evidence, and the safest design depends on maintainer intent for audit storage, plugin API scope, privacy, and whether external tools are sufficient.

options.title: Design core/plugin audit seam
options.body: Define a narrow persistence/memory write audit seam first, then implement memory-core audit records on top of it with docs and tests.

options.title: Keep memory-core-only
options.body: Implement audit records only for bundled memory-core writes, which is narrower but may leave plugins and other durable writes without a shared contract.

options.title: Defer to external plugins
options.body: Close only after maintainers decide external Pinchy/world-model-style audit plugins are the intended supported path for this capability.

recommendation.title: Design core/plugin audit seam
recommendation.body: Define a narrow persistence/memory write audit seam first, then implement memory-core audit records on top of it with docs and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue already has a prior product/security keep-open review from steipete, while the code-history trail points to adjacent memory implementation owners for follow-up.
